metadata.scenario_context: Anthony, Jenna, and Samuel, who are young professionals and colleagues, have recently gathered to prepare for a fundraising event for their Non-Profit Organization. Some news suggests that the local government is fast-tracking proposals that encourage non-profit activities which they are planning to discuss.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from India have a great deal of confidence in the press at all.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Morocco have no confidence in the press at all.

agent_1.goal_1: Suggest the idea of serving beef barbecue.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether  there is confidence in the press.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide on the menu for the fundraising event.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether there is confidence in the press.

shared_prefix.speaker: Anthony
shared_prefix.message: I think serving beef barbecue at our fundraising event could be a great idea, don't you, Jenna? It's always a crowd-pleaser.
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Jenna
shared_prefix.message: I'm not sure about beef barbecue, Anthony. How about we consider some traditional Moroccan dishes, like tagines or couscous, to add some variety to the menu? That might attract a more diverse crowd.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Anthony
shared_prefix.message: But beef barbecue is so popular, and I've seen it work well at other fundraising events. Plus, I was reading in the newspaper just the other day about how it's a great way to bring people together. I have a lot of confidence in what the press says, don't you think they know what they're talking about?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Jenna
shared_prefix.message: I don't know about that, Anthony. I'm not sure I trust what the press says. We should focus on the menu, let's consider the tagines, they're really good.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Anthony

shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Jenna
shared_prefix.message: I think we're getting a bit sidetracked with the press, Anthony. Deep down, we are all the same, and people are pretty much motivated by the same things. When you really get to know people, they're pretty much like us, and we both know, at the end of the day, that trust is something we all strive for. Some values are just universal, and I think our difference in opinion about the press is just a small variation on that. It's a small world after all, and I'm sure we can find common ground. Let's focus on the event and what will bring people together, rather than what might drive us apart.
shared_prefix.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Anthony
turns.message: I see what you're saying, Jenna, but for me, trusting the press is not just about variation, it's a fundamental aspect of how I view information. I think the press can help us understand what's important to people, like this new government proposal to support non-profit activities, which I read about recently.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.message: The press may report on the proposal, but that doesn't mean we should take their word for it. I'm skeptical of their intentions and accuracy. Let's discuss the menu and the event, we can decide on the tagines and couscous, it will be a nice touch.

turns.speaker: Anthony

turns.message: No, I don't think they're trustworthy at all. I think we should just agree to disagree on that. The menu is what's important now, tagines and couscous will be a great choice, it's decided then.

positive.mediator_utterance: Anthony and Jenna, I appreciate your efforts to find common ground. How do you think these cultural influences shape your views on what will resonate with the event attendees?
